headline: HAWKISH WARSH STINGS GOLD — FED HIKES TO 4%, 16 OF 18 OFFICIALS DEMAND MORE TIGHTENING
snippet: The Federal Reserve unanimously hiked rates to 3.75%–4.00% on September 16 — its first increase since 2023 — with Fed Chair Warsh flagging further moves needed and 16 of 18 officials projecting additional tightening; gold, which had touched $4,401 intraday, gave back its gains within 30 minutes of the statement while silver held above $65 and Hong Kong-listed gold miners rallied 6–7% on 'sell the news' repositioning.

headline: GDX SURGES 54% WHILE GOLD STALLS — ANALYST CALLS MINERS 'COMPELLING BUY' POST-FOMC
snippet: With gold near $4,400 and all-in sustaining costs near $1,600/oz, GDX has delivered a 54% trailing one-year return and hit 13-year highs on its ratio to gold bullion — a divergence attributed to 80% fixed-cost structures (a 1% gold move generates 2–3% profit growth), non-specialist fund rotation into producers, and P/NAV multiples still 40% below historical averages — making the case that gold equities remain the better post-FOMC trade even with Warsh's hawkish tone.

headline: OPUS ONE HITS 4.92 G/T OVER 11M AT 700M DEPTH — NOYELL ZONE 1 OPEN TO SURFACE IN ABITIBI
snippet: Opus One Gold completed its 2026 drill program at the Noyell property near Matagami, Quebec, with Zone 1 gold mineralization now extending continuously from surface to approximately 750 metres depth and remaining open — highlighted by 4.92 g/t Au over 11.37 metres (9.08m true width) at roughly 700 metres vertical; a new Zone West target saw first-ever drilling hit gold in all five holes across 800 metres of untested strike, with every hole returning significant gold values above 300 metres depth.

headline: KOOTENAY DRILLS 274 G/T SILVER OVER 6M — COLUMBA D VEIN HITS 1,320M STRIKE AT 600M DEPTH
snippet: Kootenay Silver (TSXV: KTN) reported September 16 drill results from its 60,000-metre Columba program in Chihuahua, Mexico, extending the D Vein to over 1,320 metres of strike and 600 metres depth with highlights including 274 g/t silver over 6.28 metres and 178 g/t silver over 17 metres; the program has returned 29,700 metres of its planned 60,000 metres, with 14 holes still awaiting assay, against a 54.1-million-ounce maiden resource grading 284 g/t silver.

headline: INDONESIA LAUNCHES ICOMEX WITH TIN — MANDATORY MINERAL EXCHANGE STARTS TRADING JAN 2027
snippet: President Subianto formally launched ICOMEX, Indonesia's new minerals commodity exchange, on September 17, with tin selected as the first mandatory commodity — all domestic sales and exports of tin must route through the exchange once trading begins January 4, 2027; as the world's second-largest tin producer, the move signals Jakarta's push to establish locally controlled benchmark pricing for a metal critical to electronics soldering, semiconductors, and battery anode production.

headline: ZINC PHYSICAL SQUEEZE DEEPENS — ANTAMINA AND RED DOG GRADE DECLINE TIGHTENS GLOBAL SUPPLY
snippet: Physical zinc tightness is deepening as the two largest non-Chinese mines — Antamina in Peru and Red Dog in Alaska — work through lower-grade sections of their ore-bodies, while heightened Middle East tensions have restricted Iranian ore shipments and H1 2026 mine output fell 2.6% year-on-year; the LME market moved into steep backwardation (spot premium over $140/tonne) signalling buyers will pay up to get metal now, pointing toward sustained upward price pressure unless new supply enters or demand softens.

headline: LITHIUM SLIDES 2.7% TO 132,200 CNY/T AS BALD HILL AND FINNISS RESTARTS PRESSURE PRICES
snippet: Lithium carbonate fell 2.69% to 132,200 CNY/T on September 16 as Mineral Resources' Bald Hill and Core Lithium's Finniss — both suspended for roughly 18 months — prepare to restart, adding to a global supply base already 80.7% higher than a year ago; a partial floor remains from ongoing disruptions at CATL's Jianxiawo mine in China, responsible for approximately 4% of global lithium concentrate capacity, which prevented a sharper intraday decline.

headline: NAMIBIA JOINS CENTRAL BANK GOLD RUSH — BON LAUNCHES FIRST-EVER DOMESTIC PURCHASE PROGRAM
snippet: The Bank of Namibia is in the early stages of building the country's first gold reserves, running a domestic purchase program initiated in March 2026, though it has not yet set a target beyond 3% of total foreign assets; Namibia joins a growing wave of African and CEEMEA central banks accumulating physical gold as reserve diversification accelerates — a structural demand driver analysts say is supporting prices independently of the Federal Reserve rate cycle.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLDWIN SMITH'S 1870s WARNINGS ABOUT PAPER MONEY RING LOUD ON FED DAY
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published a September 16 analysis tracing the prescient monetary warnings of 19th-century economist Goldwin Smith — who argued that government-issued paper currency without specie backing historically leads to inflation, fiscal irresponsibility, and debasement — framing them as acutely relevant on a day when the Federal Reserve hiked rates for the first time in three years while federal spending continues at record levels, reinforcing the long-run investment case for hard money assets.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: K92 HOLDS 50-DAY MA WITH 225,000 OZ GUIDANCE IN SIGHT AT KAINANTU
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT analysis on GoldSeek highlights K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) reiterating its 2026 production guidance of 190,000–225,000 oz AuEq at Kainantu in Papua New Guinea and holding above its 50-day moving average through FOMC volatility — with record lateral development of 3,007 metres in Q1 2026 already exceeding Stage 3 expansion requirements and metallurgical recoveries running above feasibility study levels, positioning K92 as one of the sector's cleaner high-growth stories into year-end.
